problem: The text jumps straight to 'torque proportional to V × I × cos φ'. It never says why the cosine appears, so a student cannot see where the cos φ comes from and may think any two coils give a power-reading meter.
fix: Add one sentence: the torque is proportional to the product of the two fluxes times the sine of the angle between them. The pressure-coil flux lags the supply voltage by almost 90° (the coil is highly inductive, with a phase-adjusting device), while the current-coil flux follows the current. The angle between the fluxes is therefore (90° − φ), and sin(90° − φ) = cos φ, so the torque is proportional to V × I × cos φ, which is the power P.

problem: N was defined as the number of disc revolutions, but the next sentence calls it 'the number of turns N'. Turns usually means coil turns in this chapter, so the word collides with the coil description.
fix: Say 'the number of revolutions N is proportional to energy' and keep the word 'turns' only for coil windings.

problem: Only live-to-earth and live-to-neutral tests are listed. The standard insulation test of an installation also includes neutral to earth, and leaving it out makes the procedure look complete when it is not.
fix: Add: 'then between neutral and earth. Record all three readings; the lowest one counts.'

problem: 'Keep the sample rate at least twice the highest signal frequency you want to see' gives the bare Nyquist limit. At exactly twice, a sine can be located but its shape is not faithfully displayed, and real waveforms contain harmonics well above the fundamental.
fix: Write: 'The sample rate must be more than twice the highest frequency component in the signal, harmonics included, or the display aliases. Twice is only the theoretical minimum; in practice use five to ten times the highest component for a clean shape.'

problem: 'Use a differential probe or an isolation transformer' does not say which device is isolated. A student may isolate the oscilloscope itself, which floats the earthed chassis and the probe ground clip and creates a shock hazard instead of removing one.
fix: Write: 'Use a differential probe, or feed the circuit under test through an isolation transformer, so that the point you clip to is not at a dangerous potential. Never rely on floating the oscilloscope chassis.'
